A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Anchors acceleration research, with substantial methodological revision and a new title. Text, equations, algorithms, tables and figures are readable throughout. v1 ends with references; v2's appendices and final-page experimental figures are present and readable.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original runtime and sampling experiments across three datasets, plus fidelity experiments on Adult, in Tables 2–4 and Figures 3–4.

after.justification: Section 4, Table 2 and Figures 3–6 report original runtime, sampling, precision, coverage and rule-length results, including experiments presented in the appendix.

M1.justification: v1 precomputes rules on K-means representatives and initializes explanations from the nearest representative. v2 replaces this with initially empty, similarity-thresholded memory: misses run Anchors and cache intermediate rules, while hits transform and refine cached rules (Algorithms 1–3). The reported refinement procedure also revises its stopping condition and final rule-selection criterion.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Adult income prediction, RT-Polarity sentiment classification and ImageNet-subset image classification. Changes concern sample counts and evaluation procedures within these retained datasets and tasks.

E2.justification: Original Anchors remains the sole evaluated comparison method. RF, NN, GBT, Llama 2 7B and YOLOv8 retain their corresponding roles as models being explained. The newly discussed Mor et al. method is not experimentally compared.

E3.justification: Offline pretraining-size sweeps are replaced by shuffled sequential evaluation of the memory-based method. Adult examples change from 12,345 to 1,600, RT-Polarity comments from 12,520 to 2,100, and ImageNet images from 500 to 2,000. v2 specifies a similarity threshold of 0.6 and adds rule length as an understandability metric; the 0.8 and 0.95 precision thresholds are retained.

E4.justification: v1's pretraining-size sensitivity analyses and 20-input Llama runtime case study are removed. v2 adds cold-start analyses across all six model/task combinations, plotting average runtime and sampling against processed-input count in appendix Figures 4–5 and reporting cold-start completion within 100 inputs per category.

E5.justification: v1 already displays boxplot variation and specifies ten repetitions for its 20-input case study. v2 newly reports runtime means with 95% confidence intervals in Table 2, gives additional uncertainty summaries for Llama fidelity and length, and specifies shuffle seed 42. It does not explain confidence-interval construction or establish an increase in repeated runs.

E6.justification: Under the changed protocols, Llama's reported speedup and sampling reduction change from 1.69× and 42% at N=2000 in v1 Table 3 to 8.74× and 87% in v2 Table 2; these are not matched-setting performance gains. v2 replaces the N-indexed results with aggregate runtimes and cold-start outcomes, adds text/image fidelity results, and reports rule lengths across all tasks.

T1.justification: v2 adds Section 3.5's memory-miss complexity derivation and assumptions supporting negligible retrieval overhead. It also replaces v1's simple vertical-transformation precision constraint with a probability-constrained maximum-coverage definition. The newly explicit conditional-distribution equation in Definition 2.2 omits normalization.

C1.justification: The main contribution changes from offline representative-rule pretraining to MAnchors' online memorization and reuse of intermediate rules. The introduction and conclusion additionally emphasize overcoming caching limitations and reducing LLM sampling and monetary costs. The general aim of accelerating Anchors while preserving explanation quality remains.

C2.justification: v1 explains weaker text/Llama acceleration through embedding dimensionality and complex decision boundaries, and proposes larger pretraining sets to recover coverage. v2 explains its strongest Llama acceleration through expensive model queries and weaker gains elsewhere through model efficiency and cold-start costs. It newly discusses rule-length degradation and increasing the similarity threshold to improve explanation quality at the expense of longer cold starts.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents k-d-tree retrieval, delta=0.6, the similarity threshold and grid-search selection criteria. Section 4.1 and Appendix A disclose four 24GB GPUs, 256GB system memory and approximately 300 hours of experiments. These add reproducibility information, although confidence-interval construction and several implementation specifics remain unstated.

R1.justification: v1's broad assertion that no effective Anchors acceleration method exists is replaced by a substantive comparison with Mor et al. (2024), distinguishing global aggregation from instance-specific explanations. This materially revises the novelty positioning. v2 also adds application, target-model and complexity-analysis citations while removing references associated with K-means and ResNet50.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, background, method exposition and experimental narrative undergo extensive rewriting. The introductory image example moves into the approach overview, and the method is reorganized around workflow, memory misses, memory hits and overhead analysis. v2 also adds impact, compute-resource and LLM-use sections.

P2.justification: The Anchors workflow diagram is retained and renumbered, while the car-based transformation illustration is redrawn using cats and memory terminology. Three pretraining-size result tables become one table with runtimes and confidence intervals. The experimental displays are substantially redesigned into a main-text Llama boxplot and appendix runtime, sampling and fidelity/length panels.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses v1's tabular-only fidelity evidence with quality measurements across all tasks, and adds aggregate runtimes, confidence intervals and cold-start analyses. However, new Definition 2.2 lacks normalization, and Algorithm 3's final maximum-coverage selection omits the precision filter, unlike v1's return of the precision-tested rule. These inconsistencies affect the central fidelity claim. The PDFs do not resolve whether they are specification errors or affect the evaluated procedure, preventing a reliable net-quality judgment.
